§6Wood Oil§f

§aFully renewable from trees - crack it into heating oil, mix it into biofuel, or dye things!§f

Wood Oil is a viscous, flammable, polluting liquid at §e110 kTU§f per bucket. It is produced from wood products in the §bCombination Oven§f, making it one of the few fully renewable petrochemical feedstocks.

§6Production§f (Combination Oven):
§b•§f Sawdust Briquette → Charcoal + §e500mB§f Wood Oil.
§b•§f Oak Wood → Charcoal + §e250mB§f.
§b•§f Spruce Sapling → Wood Ash + §e50mB§f.

§6Uses§f:
§b•§f Cracking Tower: §e100mB§f + §e200mB§f Steam → §e40mB§f Heating Oil + §e10mB§f Aromatic Hydrocarbons.
§b•§f Biofuel: §e500mB§f + §e500mB§f Fish Oil / Sunflower Seed Oil → §e1,000mB§f Biofuel.
§b•§f Wood Tar: §e1,000mB§f → §e1×§f (Industrial Solidification Machine).
§b•§f Coker Unit: §e3,000mB§f → Charcoal + §e300mB§f Coker Gas.
§b•§f Chemical Dyes: Ore Acidizer with powders.

§ePS:§f Wood Oil is excellent for §bbiofuel§f and early polymer crafting. A single stack of wood through the Combination Oven yields hundreds of buckets. Combine with the §bStirling Sawmill§f for maximum log-to-oil efficiency!
